teams.heading: Fiji seek defensive stability after conceding 326 points in 11 matches
teams.body: The Flying Fijians go into the international break looking to arrest a three-match losing streak following their 17-33 defeat against Scotland in Round three. Across their last 11 games, the national side has scored 315 points while conceding 326, producing high-scoring averages of 28.6 and 29.6 per match respectively. Although Fiji sits 12th on the log with a -96 points difference, the team previously showed its clinical edge in a 63-10 win over Canada in September 2025.

teams.heading: Henry Pollock weighs up Super League switch following Eddie Hearn's valuation demand
teams.body: England prospect Henry Pollock is reportedly weighing up a cross-code switch to Super League following claims that his off-field profile could command a significant salary. The move comes as pundits debate Eddie Hearn’s reported million-pound valuation for the youngster, a figure some labelled "laughable" for a Premiership player. While Steve Borthwick has faced pressure since July to integrate Pollock into his starting XV, the ongoing uncertainty regarding his contract and league interest remains unresolved before November's tests.

teams.heading: France sit third in the Nations Championship after their Japan victory
teams.body: France currently occupy third place in the Nations Championship table following their 42-15 victory against Japan in the previous round. Fabien Galthié's side have recorded two wins and one loss from their three fixtures to date, amassing 116 points while conceding 75. The squad now look ahead to their next meeting with Fiji, whom they defeated 34-21 during an international friendly in November 2025. France enter the autumn window with a positive points difference of 41 across the tournament so far.

teams.heading: Former Ireland enforcer Ryan Caldwell reveals harrowing descent into addiction and prison
teams.body: Former Ireland second-row Ryan Caldwell has detailed his harrowing descent into drug addiction and a period of incarceration following his retirement from the professional game. In a sobering interview ahead of the release of his autobiography, *White Lines*, the former Ulster enforcer reflects on the impact of chronic pain and a final major concussion that triggered a spiral of suicidal depression. Now a meditation teacher in Belfast, the 42-year-old’s account provides a stark perspective on the transition out of the sport as the national side prepares for November.

teams.heading: Andrea Zambonin signs new Exeter contract while recovering from shoulder surgery
teams.body: Lock Andrea Zambonin has committed his long-term future to Exeter Chiefs, signing a contract extension while he continues his recovery. The Italy international remains sidelined following major shoulder surgery and is expected to miss the start of the new Premiership season. Although the injury prevented his involvement in recent Nations Championship fixtures, the second-row remains a central figure in the national setup. While no specific return date is confirmed, he is working to be fit for the upcoming November internationals.

teams.heading: Alun Wyn Jones joins Ospreys board as golden generation stars confirm careers
teams.body: The transition of Wales’ "second golden generation" into life after rugby continues, with Alun Wyn Jones recently confirmed as a new board member at the Ospreys. Jones, the world’s most-capped player, has also taken a strategic advisory post at Swansea University alongside his ongoing punditry work. He is joined in the Ospreys’ setup by former teammate Justin Tipuric, who now serves as the region’s defence coach. Their moves come as the current national side sits ninth in the standings following a 0-43 defeat to South Africa.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One Settles Dispute Over Player Eligibility Criteria
teams.body: The JRLO has formally amended its 2026-2027 registration system following a court-backed settlement with 25 players, including several Japan internationals. The league faced a legal challenge regarding proposed category splits, which critics argued discriminated against naturalised athletes. Under the revised framework, players with 30 or more Brave Blossoms caps will be reclassified from A-2 to the premier A-1 category. The league acknowledged that “prior explanations and communication with all relevant parties were insufficient” regarding the initial implementation.

While some pundits have called for retrospective sanctions, Carter remained lighthearted about the exchange, noting the two may face off again during Saturday’s third encounter in Soweto as the series remains level at 1-1.

teams.body: Former Springboks coach Nick Mallett has backed Rassie Erasmus following his heated response to claims that South Africa’s scrum is illegal. Mallett insisted that the Bok pack’s dominance is legitimate and technical, rather than a result of foul play. Erasmus recently expressed frustration at the media narrative surrounding the set-piece, arguing that his counterpart, Dave Rennie, should have utilised official World Rugby protocols to raise grievances rather than airing opinions in post-match briefings.
